attachment_note: The three named PNGs under figure-previews-e138d27ca/ were opened and read as images, and nothing else was opened: no SVG and no image besides them. Each attachment carries its figure's basename, so the mapping is by filename rather than by order. Every measurement below was taken from the pixels of these PNGs at their rendered size of 1960x1008. The captions were read from docs/evidence/fragments/diiid-vertical-force-balance/diiid-frame-146-vertical-loss.html at the reviewed head: each states numbers the figure does not carry (trip-1 axis Z=-0.346 m, 0.912xIp confined; trip-2 axis Z=+1.556 m above the limiter top at +1.363 m, 0.046xIp confined, 39 mask entries changed; frame-137 axis Z=-0.361 m, 0.737xIp confined, 20 mask entries), so none is a restatement of the figure title.

findings.disposition: folded: a figure-family follow-up drawing the solved-flux legend key at SOLVED_FLUX_WIDTH so the key weight matches the field the figure exists to show, in every panel of the set
findings.summary: The solved-flux legend key is drawn at the median of the per-level stroke widths, so the key that names the panel's subject inherits whatever the crowding rule did to this particular field. In the frame-146-trip-2 PNG the key renders as a single-row stroke (blue pixels at x478-526, y30 only, 49 px), while the same key on the two sibling panels is a 6 px band (x438-490 / x402-454, y28-33, 317 and 316 px). A reader comparing the three panels sees the key change weight from a bold line to a hairline, and on the trip-2 panel cannot match a 1 px key to the contour set at a glance. The key states the series identity, so it should carry the headline weight in every panel of the set.

findings.disposition: exempted: the missing interior solved ink is the field's own state rather than a rendering fault, the caption states the collapse and the lifted axis, and the stroke and key weights are recorded separately under finding 1
findings.summary: The grey EFIT reference carries 6.3x the ink of the blue solved subject in the panel box (49,440 grey px against 7,825 blue px), where the two sibling panels run the other way (27,867 grey against 43,075 blue, and 28,259 against 44,088). Every solved level on this panel is near the 0.7 pt floor the crowding rule sets, and the surviving blue falls in two fans at the top and bottom edges with none in the core, so the panel alone reads as an EFIT plot with a blue fringe. The absence is the reported collapse (0.046xIp confined, axis lifted to Z=+1.556 m) and the caption states it in words, so a reader who reads the caption misreads nothing; the weight inversion is what the reader sees first.

findings.disposition: exempted: the column is about 230 px wide and carries up to six tick labels, so 12 pt keeps them clear of the axis label and of each other on all three panels, and legibility is verified on the rendered PNGs rather than assumed
findings.summary: The residual column's tick labels are set to 12 pt while the two axis labels beside them are 14 pt, and the plotting rules give tick labels 14 pt. All three PNGs render the ticks legibly and consistently with each other (0.00 to 0.15 at 0.05 on the frame-137 panel, 0.00 to 0.25 on both frame-146 panels, now one precision and one step across the set), and no label collides, so nothing is lost to a reader; the size is simply one step below the rest of the figure's text.
